Name: Croque-monsieur
Description: Grilled ham and cheese sandwich topped with béchamel, baked until golden; classic Parisian café snack.

Name: Paris-Brest
Description: Ring-shaped choux pastry filled with praline‑flavored cream, created for the 1891 Paris–Brest–Paris race and remains a beloved French pâtisserie.

Name: Soupe à l'oignon Gratinée
Description: Rich beef broth onion soup topped with toasted baguette and melted cheese, traditionally served in Paris bistros.

Name: Papeda
Description: Sago starch porridge, smooth and gelatinous, served with hot fish broth and shredded fish; staple of West Papua.

Name: Ikan Bakar Sorong
Description: Grilled tuna marinated in lime, chilies, and local herbs, commonly sold at Sorong’s waterfront fish stalls.

Name: Sate Tuna
Description: Skewered tuna brushed with sweet soy and chili glaze, grilled over coconut husk charcoal, popular in Sorong night markets.

Name: Salmorejo
Description: Thick cold tomato soup with bread, olive oil, garlic, topped with diced jamón and hard‑boiled egg.

Name: Espinacas con garbanzos
Description: Sautéed spinach cooked with chickpeas, garlic, cumin and a splash of sherry, typical Seville tapa.

Name: Huevos a la flamenca
Description: Baked eggs in tomato sauce with chorizo, peas, ham and peppers, served as a hearty Seville specialty.

Name: Sydney rock oysters
Description: Fresh Sydney rock oysters, shucked and served raw on the half shell, harvested from the harbour.

Name: Balmain Bug
Description: Balmain Bug, sand crab grilled with garlic butter, a popular seafood specialty from Sydney’s Balmain harbour.

Name: Monjayaki
Description: Savory pan‑fried batter with cabbage, seafood, and soy sauce, cooked and eaten at the table.

Name: Edomae sushi
Description: Nigiri sushi using fresh tuna, eel, and seasoned rice, reflecting Edo‑era fish‑market tradition in Tokyo.

Name: Tokyo shoyu ramen
Description: Clear soy‑based broth with wavy noodles, chashu, menma, and scallions, exemplifying classic Tokyo ramen style.

Name: New York–style pizza
Description: Thin, foldable crust pizza topped with tomato sauce, mozzarella, often sold by the slice in NYC pizzerias.

Name: New York–style bagel
Description: Dense, boiled‑then‑baked bagel with a shiny crust, traditionally topped with sesame or poppy seeds, eaten citywide.

Name: New York–style cheesecake
Description: Rich, creamy cheesecake on a graham‑crust base, often flavored with vanilla, a staple of NYC dessert menus.

Name: Manhattan clam chowder
Description: Tomato‑based chowder with clams, potatoes, carrots, and celery, reflecting New York’s coastal influences distinct from New England.

Name: Feijoada à carioca
Description: Hearty black‑bean stew with pork, beef, and sausages, served with rice, collard greens, orange slices; Rio’s classic weekend dish.

Name: Biscoito Globo
Description: Salty, cheese‑flavored cracker, crisp and airy, sold at Copacabana and Ipanema beaches; iconic Rio snack.

Name: Cachorro‑quente carioca
Description: Street hot dog topped with corn, peas, potatoes, ketchup, mustard, mayo, and melted cheese; Rio’s beloved street fare.

Name: Hawawshi
Description: Spiced minced meat baked inside baladi flatbread, created in Cairo and sold as street‑food specialty.

Name: Fatta
Description: Rice layered with crispy flatbread, garlic‑tomato sauce and boiled meat, traditionally served at Cairo celebrations.

Name: Koshary
Description: Lentils, rice, pasta, chickpeas topped with tomato sauce and fried onions, iconic Cairo street dish.

Name: Moscow Salad
Description: Moscow Salad – a Russian salad with diced boiled potatoes, carrots, pickles, ham, peas, and mayonnaise, known as "Moscow" variant.

Name: Moscow Cutlet
Description: Moscow Cutlet – pan‑fried ground meat patty mixed with bread crumbs, onions, and spices, traditionally served with potatoes.
